title: Why India is betting big on semiconductors

scenes.text: India wants to make the chip inside your next phone.
scenes.sub: Here's why that's a bigger deal than it sounds.

scenes.text: Over 90% of advanced chips come from just two countries.
scenes.narration: Over ninety percent of advanced chips come from just two countries — Taiwan and South Korea.

scenes.text: India has committed to building its own chip industry from scratch.
scenes.narration: India has committed seventy six thousand crore rupees to building its own chip industry, from scratch.

scenes.text: First fab plants are coming up in Gujarat and Assam.
scenes.narration: First fab plants are coming up in Gujarat and Assam.

scenes.text: Chips don't just run phones — they run cars, hospitals, and defence systems.
scenes.narration: Chips don't just run phones. They run cars, hospitals, and defence systems.

scenes.text: This creates hundreds of thousands of high-skill jobs: design engineers, fab technicians, process specialists.
If you're in engineering, or considering it —
scenes.sub: semiconductors might be the most under-the-radar career bet of this decade.
